text.content:
This part follows an Awakened or Emerged character from the sheet to the chat card: casting a spell, summoning and binding a spirit, going astral, leading a ritual, initiating, then, for technomancers, threading a complex form and compiling a sprite. It is meant for the player who plays a magician, an adept or a technomancer, and for the GM who wants to know what the system checks on its own and what is left for them to decide.

The rules themselves stay in the book: each chapter gives the page where to read them. What the system automates beyond the core rulebook (supplements, options) is flagged with its source.

All

What it is for

Casting a spell takes three gestures: a click on the spell's dice pool, a choice of Force in the roll window, then the buttons of the chat card (resist Drain, have the target defend or resist, apply the effect). The system computes the pool, the Limit and the Drain, takes into account active foci, sustained spells and reagents, and offers what comes next to the right character.

  • ① Magic type and initiate grade: Magician, Adept, Mystical Adept or Aspected Magician. As long as this field stays on None, the sheet shows neither tradition nor Drain resistance: set it first.

  • ② The tradition: the Magical Tradition item gives the Drain resistance attribute and the spirit types of the five spell categories (@UUID[.1yG7AM03EulpiQqD]{spirits}).

  • ③ The astral plane: astral perception, Drain Resistance, astral defense… (@UUID[.DZqLEimyQwylLGta]{the astral}).

  • ④ Reagents: your stock of drams, and the button used to harvest them (@UUID[.lFDbnVCRn4ClwA6w]{rituals, preparations, reagents}).

  • ⑤ Spells: click the figure in the DP (dice pool) column to cast the spell.

  • ⑥ Force and hits of the last casting (F and H columns): the system fills them in at the roll; you can correct them with a click (right-click to increase, left-click to decrease).

  • ⑦ Sustaining (Dur. column): the icon switches the sustaining of a sustained-duration spell on or off.

  • ⑧ Foci: the Equip pin activates a focus; its rating is set with a click.

  • ⑨ Metamagics: the Activate Metamagic pin puts its effects into play (@UUID[.zibQ5EI5pAW7Wv7E]{initiation}).

Step by step: casting a spell

  1. If the spell targets someone, first target their token (right-click the token, then Toggle Target State, see @UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.UtP5ShuRjXa3JrEZ.JournalEntryPage.9jXWevgNpySvo7Wz]{the token HUD}).

  2. On the sheet, open the magic tab and click the spell's dice pool, in the DP column. The Cast Spell window opens.

  3. Choose the Force with the − and + buttons. It starts from your Magic; the Limit and the Final Drain, at the bottom of the window, follow at once (Core Rulebook p. 281-282).

  4. Tick the options if needed: Reckless spellcasting (Drain goes up by 3), Reagents (the number of drams replaces the Limit), SpellShaping for an area spell if you have the metamagic.

  5. Click Roll Dice. The spell's card arrives in the chat with your hits.

  6. Click Resist Drain on the card: the figure in brackets is the Drain to resist. The system rolls your resistance and ticks the boxes, Stun or Physical according to the rule (Core Rulebook p. 282).

  7. The target then does its part from the same card: Defend against an indirect spell, Resisting (Direct Spell) against a direct spell, or nothing at all for a spell that is not resisted. For a spell that sets an effect (an increase, an armor…), click Apply Effect.

The Aura of [element] spells (Fire Aura, Lightning Aura…) set two effects on their subject: their melee attacks gain +1 DV per hit and become elemental, and whoever touches them in melee resists a DV equal to the hits, in the element (Street Grimoire p. 115).

  • ① Base Dice Pool and ② Modifiers: unfold them (the arrow) to see the detail, foci and penalties included.

  • ③ Force: the only mandatory choice.

  • ④ Casting options: reckless spellcasting, reagents, shaping.

  • ⑤ Final Drain and ⑥ Limit: recomputed at each change.

  • ⑦ Roll Dice, or ⑧ Push the Limit to spend a point of Edge before the roll (Core Rulebook p. 56).

@UUID[.jaRKuOQo9qZOsEmZ]{Area spells} →

An area spell shows its range with an (A) and, after casting, its radius in meters. On the card, the target-shaped icon places the template on the scene: it is the template that says who is hit. For a detection spell, the radius is the Force multiplied by your Magic, and ten times more at extended range (Core Rulebook p. 285).

An indirect Combat area spell is cast like a grenade, with a threshold of 3 (Core Rulebook p. 283). With no hit at all, it fails. With one or two hits, it scatters: the card carries the Scatter button, which moves the template, and nobody defends. From three hits, the target defends normally and the DV takes the net hits into account.

Shaping: the bubbles

The SpellShaping line only appears if the metamagic is active on the sheet. It has two fields, extra radius and spared characters, which share a cap equal to your Magic, Shaping focus included (Core Rulebook p. 326, 320); the dice are removed from your pool. On the card, a button designates the spared tokens (targeted or selected): they get no defense, no resistance and no effect from the spell. When your targets and your selection differ, a window has you tick the characters to spare.

A one-meter bubble cannot be drawn on a grid: the system counts "one point spares one character". This rate is a GM setting, Spell Shaping: cost of one bubble (Magic tab), because the book gives no conversion.

pages.name: Sustaining a spell, foci and counterspelling

text.content:
A sustained-duration spell (S in the Dur. column) is sustained with a click on its icon; a second click releases it. While it is sustained, the system counts the sustaining penalty on your rolls (Core Rulebook p. 282). For someone other than you to sustain it, a sustaining focus does the job: choose the spell in its sheet.

A focus only acts if it is Equipped (the pin on its line). The system then adds its rating where it counts: a spellcasting focus to the spells of its category, a power focus to your Magic, hence to all your magic pools (Core Rulebook p. 318-320). It only keeps one per use, the most powerful, with one exception: a power focus stacks with a spell focus, without its bonus counting twice in the same test. Bonding foci (the Karma spent) is kept on the sheet, by hand.

The Counterspelling line of your skills carries two figures: on the left, the Spell defense dice pool you have built up (right-click to increase it, left-click to decrease it), on the right the cap the skill gives you (Core Rulebook p. 294). These dice are then spent by hand, when an ally or you yourself resist a spell. A counterspelling focus adds its Force. The GM removes the bonus in the roll window if the spell's category does not match the focus's.

Blocked by the system?

When the system refuses a gesture (a spell under Blight, shaping beyond your Magic…), it is a rule lock of the Magic family. The GM can lift it in Shadowrun settings, Presets tab, Set the locks button: the action then goes through, and the GM is warned (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.arMGpK6RvbR3sLNQ.JournalEntryPage.yj32FTBiKvVIyGIf]{the rule locks}).

← @UUID[.jaRKuOQo9qZOsEmZ]{Area spells} · @UUID[.55CfHCBIRElkTLWi]{Related settings and references} →

What the system does on its own

  • It computes the pool (Spellcasting + Magic), the Limit (the Force) and the Drain, with active foci, the sustained spells penalty and wounds.

  • It chooses Physical or Stun damage for Drain according to your hits and your Magic.

  • It offers the target the right response (defense or resistance), and the template of an area spell.

  • It removes the drams spent and never lets the stock go below 0.

What the GM does by hand

  • The placement of a template enlarged by shaping, and the bonding of foci.

  • The glitch of a casting, when the book leaves them the choice of its effects (Core Rulebook p. 282).

  • The bonus of a counterspelling focus from another category than the spell, to remove in the roll window.

All

What it is for

The system follows a spirit from its summoning to its departure: it rolls the Summoning test and the spirit's resistance, counts the services, creates the spirit on the magician's sheet, then, with a click, the actor that plays it on the scene. Binding and banishing follow the same path. The GM keeps control of what the book entrusts to them: reputation with spirits, free spirits, wild spirits.

Step by step: summoning a spirit

  1. On the sheet, Active Skills tab, click the dice pool (DP column) of the Summoning skill.

  2. In the window, under Summoning options, choose the Force and the Spirit Type: the list offers the five types of your tradition (Core Rulebook p. 300).

  3. Click Roll Dice. The chat card shows your hits and the Spirit Resistance button, which only the GM sees.

  4. The GM clicks it: the spirit's resistance is rolled (its Force in dice), then a second card appears with Resist Drain and, if you have at least one net hit, Summon Spirit; otherwise it shows Failed Summon.

  5. Click Resist Drain, then Summon Spirit. A message confirms the summoning, and the spirit joins the Summoned Spirits block of the magic tab, with as many services as net hits (Core Rulebook p. 300).

The name or the pool?

On a skill's line, the name opens a test where you choose the attribute; the figure in the DP column opens the full test, with the book's attribute (Magic for Conjuring skills). To summon, bind or banish, click the figure.

pages.name: The spirit on the sheet, then on the scene

text.content:
Each line of the Summoned Spirits block carries the spirit's type and Force. Services are counted down with a click (left click to remove one, right click to add one). The Call spirit button creates the spirit's actor, with its attributes, skills and powers computed from its Force and type; place its token on the scene from the actors tab. The same button, which has become the dismiss button, deletes that actor when the spirit leaves.

When you play the spirit, its roll window offers you your own Edge, as long as you have some left: the summoner can spend it on their spirits' tests (Core Rulebook p. 303).

In the header, the Bound Spirit icon sits next to the materialization one, with its tooltip. The default layout of a spirit sheet shows the Qualities (traits) and Vision types blocks; a spirit whose layout the GM customized keeps its own, and the GM adds the traits block if it is missing.

Step by step: binding a spirit

  1. Target the token of the spirit to bind.

  2. Click the dice pool of the Binding skill. The window ticks Reagents and offers Force × 25 drams (Core Rulebook p. 301); if your stock is not enough, a warning says so.

  3. Roll the dice. The GM clicks Spirit Resistance: the spirit resists with twice its Force.

  4. On the resistance card, click Bind Spirit: the Bounded column switches to "Yes" and the services gained are added. Then resist Drain from your card.

Banishing follows the same path: target the spirit, click the Banishing dice pool, and the GM has the spirit resist from the card (Core Rulebook p. 301).

Backlinks: @UUID[.n57naBPmfmmiiOB3]{MENU} > @UUID[.1yG7AM03EulpiQqD]{4.2 Spirits}

← @UUID[.1yG7AM03EulpiQqD]{4.2 Spirits} · @UUID[.9iBwKm0TOVo2IXSn]{What the GM sets on a spirit} →

pages.name: What the GM sets on a spirit

text.content:
The traits block of the spirit sheet carries five boxes that only the GM sees and ticks: Elemental, Wild, Domain, Magic pact and Free spirit. They used to be in the header, where they nearly hid the name.

  • Free spirit gives the spirit its own Edge (by default half its Force, rounded up), which the GM adjusts (Core Rulebook p. 303-304); with Magic pact, it can still draw on its former summoner's (Street Grimoire p. 137).

  • Elemental lowers its mental attributes and adds a service; Wild and Domain change its resistance to banishing and some powers (Forbidden Arcana p. 177-181).

On the magician's sheet, the Astral Reputation block (spirit index, adjustment) and the Wild Reputation block are kept by the GM; the player does not see them. Astral Reputation removes its dice from Summoning, Binding and Banishing tests; the box is ticked by default in the roll window, and only the GM can untick it (Street Grimoire p. 207). Wild Reputation gives its dice to call a wild spirit or deal with it (Forbidden Arcana p. 177).

House Rules — Book option: the spirit leash

The Spirit leash (Forbidden Arcana p. 176) setting (Magic tab of Shadowrun settings) is unticked by default. Ticked, a chain icon appears next to each summoned spirit: the taut leash counts as a sustained spell, and a spirit that gets many hits offers the GM to Test the leash (Forbidden Arcana p. 182).

Backlinks: @UUID[.n57naBPmfmmiiOB3]{MENU} > @UUID[.1yG7AM03EulpiQqD]{4.2 Spirits}

← @UUID[.gzozcTxn5gRmcqKe]{The spirit on the sheet, then on the scene} · @UUID[.1pRqO6y6Sw387LIU]{Custom spirit types and entities} →

A spirit the book does not describe (a mist spirit, a variant specific to a mentor) is created as an item: items tab, Create Item, type Spirit Type. The new type immediately joins the list of types, for summoning as well as in traditions.

  1. Open the item's configuration tab (the cog icon).

  2. Choose the official type it inherits from in Based On: it takes over its attributes, skills, initiative and powers.

  3. Enter only the differences: a Modifier is added to the attribute, a Fixed Value replaces it; add skills and powers.

  4. Check the What this type gives block, at the bottom: it shows the spirit as it would be summoned at Force 4.

The Summonable with the Summoning skill box, reserved to the GM, removes a type from the summoning list. That is how extraplanar entities are set up (an Erinye, a Kappa, a shedim): the GM creates a Spirit actor of that type and chooses its Force, without summoning (Howling Shadows p. 114). The Mégapack provides these types ready-made (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.LY0gP2n4uytah6mP.JournalEntryPage.Qp5FrYdO1ggybgHp]{the Mégapack}).

Insect spirits and the Skill power

An insect spirit's sheet, and the Spirit item, have an Insect race list: it gives the caste the powers, skills and resistance bonus of its race (subterranean termite +2, Goliath +4), the rest as a tooltip note (Dark Terrors p. 21-32). The Skill spirit power carries the skill it grants (Aetherology p. 38).

Backlinks: @UUID[.n57naBPmfmmiiOB3]{MENU} > @UUID[.1yG7AM03EulpiQqD]{4.2 Spirits}

← @UUID[.9iBwKm0TOVo2IXSn]{What the GM sets on a spirit} · @UUID[.vDsTIQNEfcFGvvE4]{Related settings and references} →

What the system does on its own

  • It rolls the spirit's resistance, counts the services, creates the spirit and its actor, gives it its powers from the compendium chosen by the GM.

  • It gives it its weapons: Unarmed (except the watcher, which has no physical form) and the weapon of each of its optional powers, chosen before the summoning or dragged onto its sheet afterwards. For an Elemental Attack, a window asks the GM for the element, even when a player summons; the fire spirit gets its own with no question. The DVs rated in Magic follow the Magic line (Core Rulebook p. 396).

  • It lists the spirit's foci in the Focus tab, when the sheet configuration adds it.

  • It removes the binding reagents and the Astral Reputation from Conjuring tests.

What the GM does by hand

  • Keeps the spirit index and decides on free, wild or elemental spirits.

  • Rules on what a spirit without services does, and on social interactions with spirits.

All

What it is for

A magician can look at the astral plane (astral perception) or go there entirely (projection). The system switches the token's vision, changes initiative and refuses what cannot be done from the astral. The GM, for their part, sets the background count of each scene, which weighs on every magic roll made there.

Step by step: switching to astral perception

  1. On the sheet, magic tab, click the pin on the Astral Perception line, in the Astral Plane block.

  2. The pin lights up. Your token switches to Astral Perception vision and carries the state of the same name: you see the astral plane within the range set by the GM (Core Rulebook p. 312-313).

  3. Click the pin again to go back to normal vision.

The same pin is found in the sheet's Vision types block, Astral Perception line, for those who perceive the astral; it is always on for a spirit (Core Rulebook p. 301). What astral perception shows on screen, and what it changes to the dice: @UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.a0A5owDWyn9339sO.JournalEntryPage.u9jjBFVO4x8wpNs8]{see 3.2}.

Step by step: projecting

  1. Open the sheet's attributes tab (the A icon) and go down to the Initiatives block.

  2. Click the pin on the Astral line. Your initiative becomes astral initiative, and the Astral Initiative effect is shown on the token (Core Rulebook p. 313).

  3. In combat, the switch costs a Complex Action; if you have none left, the system refuses it.

  4. To go back into your body, click the pin on the Physical line.

In projection, the tests that need a body are refused with the message You can't roll a Test in astral projection. The astral tests stay in the Astral Plane block: Astral Defense, Pass Through Mana Barrier, Astral Tracking; astral combat is rolled from the Astral Combat skill (Core Rulebook p. 315-316). A weapon focus can also be wielded in astral combat: the option is set on its line, in the sheet's list of weapons.

Backlinks: @UUID[.n57naBPmfmmiiOB3]{MENU}

← @UUID[.vDsTIQNEfcFGvvE4]{Related settings and references} · @UUID[.BcmXkWjJe13iV892]{A scene's background count (GM)} →

Background count is set per scene: configure the scene, Background Count tab. The value is then shown at the bottom left of the screen, next to the Matrix Noise (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.UtP5ShuRjXa3JrEZ.JournalEntryPage.o25ieQmnMSZt0yYC]{the screen at a glance}).

  • Background Count rating, from −24 to +24. Positive, it is a domain: the tradition of the Alignment gains the value as Limit, all the others lose it in dice. Negative, it is a mana ebb or void: everyone loses the value in dice, whatever their tradition (Aetherology p. 9-10) and (Aetherology p. 33).

  • Astral phenomenon (Mist, Shroud, Void, astral rift…): the list fills in the rating and the alignment with one click, in the middle of the book's range; you can then change them. The indicator's tooltip recalls what the system leaves to the GM (Aetherology p. 32-34).

  • An area spell or preparation can carry its own background count on its template; it only counts on the scene where the template is placed.

Backlinks: @UUID[.n57naBPmfmmiiOB3]{MENU} > @UUID[.DZqLEimyQwylLGta]{4.3 The astral}

← @UUID[.DZqLEimyQwylLGta]{4.3 The astral} · @UUID[.Vi6bdKuDngfOfl4x]{Grey mana and blight} →

Two items from Better Than Bad cut off magic, and the system applies them on its own (Better Than Bad p. 156-157):

  • Grey mana (armor accessory or tattoo) adds its rating to the dice to resist spells, but an Awakened character who wears it loses as many dice on their magic rolls.

  • Blight, a toxin, sets the Cut from the manasphere effect: no more spells, rituals, conjuring or astral as long as it lasts. When it strikes, sustained spells end, foci go out and a projected character comes back into their body. When the effect ends, nothing comes back on its own: switch your foci back on. Blight's refusals are a lock of the Magic family, which the GM can lift.

Backlinks: @UUID[.n57naBPmfmmiiOB3]{MENU} > @UUID[.DZqLEimyQwylLGta]{4.3 The astral}

← @UUID[.BcmXkWjJe13iV892]{A scene's background count (GM)} · @UUID[.Y484fgMYofP0u4CD]{Related settings and references} →

What the system does on its own

  • It switches the token's vision and initiative, and counts down the Complex Action of projection in combat.

  • It applies the background count of the scene and of templates to each magic roll.

What the GM does by hand

  • The time a projected character spends out of their body, the Dweller on the Threshold, mana barriers set up by a ritual.

  • The effects of an astral phenomenon that the tooltip recalls (Perception penalty, Composure test, spell deviation).

All

What it is for

A ritual is led by several people: the system opens a preparation card where each announces themselves, adds the group's help to the leader's roll, then gives each participant their own Drain button. A preparation is made from a spell marked as an alchemical formula, keeps its Potency and loses it with the world's time. Reagents are counted on the sheet, spent in the roll window and harvested with a click.

Step by step: leading a ritual (the leader)

  1. Check your stock of Reagents: without reagents, the system refuses with You don't have reagents left !.

  2. In the Rituals block of the magic tab, click the ritual's dice pool. The Perform Ritual: window asks for the Force: choose it, then Confirm. It is set before anyone rolls the dice (Core Rulebook p. 295).

  3. The "Ritual in preparation" card arrives in the chat, with Join (for everyone) and Seal (for you and the GM).

  4. When everyone has joined, click Seal: nobody else can come in, and the roll window opens with the group's help (Core Rulebook p. 296) and (Core Rulebook p. 49).

  5. Roll the dice. The GM clicks Ritual resistance; the resistance card then gives one Drain button per person (Resist Drain followed by the name) and says whether the ritual succeeds.

Step by step: joining a ritual (the participants)

  1. Select your character's token on the scene (otherwise, it is the character assigned to you who takes part).

  2. Click Join on the ritual's card. Your help roll (Ritual Spellcasting + Magic) is rolled on its own, and a card announces your participation.

  3. The card warns you of special cases: Tradition different from the leader's: -2 dice.; without the Ritual Spellcasting skill, you bring no dice but still suffer the Drain (Core Rulebook p. 295).

  4. After sealing, resist Drain with your button on the resistance card.

Two ritual keywords change the course of things (Street Grimoire p. 122): an Adept ritual is performed alone, without a preparation card; a Contractual ritual refuses sealing as long as no participant has joined. The Mana Flux and Mana Ebb rituals give the GM a button that brings the scene's background count closer to 0 for [Force] hours of game time (Shadow Spells p. 22) (@UUID[.BcmXkWjJe13iV892]{background count}).

1. Open the spell's sheet (the edit icon on its line) and tick Alchemical formula. The spell goes under the Alchemical formulae subheading of the spell list.

  2. Click its dice pool: the Create preparation window opens (Alchemy + Magic). Choose the Force and the Trigger (Command, Contact or Time) (Core Rulebook p. 304-305).

  3. Roll the dice, resist Drain. The GM clicks Preparation resistance, then you click Create preparation: the preparation joins the Preparations block, with its Potency equal to your net hits (Core Rulebook p. 305).

  4. To trigger it, click its dice pool in the Preparations block.

A preparation keeps its full Potency for (Potency × 2) hours of game time, then loses 1 point per hour; the system lowers it when the GM moves the clock forward, and a preparation at 0 can no longer be triggered (Core Rulebook p. 305). The GM can lengthen these durations on the preparation's sheet, configuration tab (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.UtP5ShuRjXa3JrEZ.JournalEntryPage.YRfJG9p6WnN6cUDi]{the clock}):

  • Full Potency: × 3 for the Lasting Preparations mastery or some traditions, × 4 for others (Forbidden Arcana p. 39, 75) and (Forbidden Arcana p. 132).

  • Loss of Potency: 1 per day (Fixation) with the Anchoring metamagic (Core Rulebook p. 326).

← @UUID[.lFDbnVCRn4ClwA6w]{4.4 Rituals, preparations, reagents} · @UUID[.pG9EwPHh1eg4H5j5]{Reagents} →

The stock is kept in the Reagents block of the magic tab: left click to remove one dram, right click to add one, Shift for ten at a time. In the window of a magic roll, the Reagents box opens the number of drams to spend: it replaces the Limit, and the stock goes down when you roll (Core Rulebook p. 316-318). The Another tradition's reagents (half) box halves the drams counted.

Step by step: harvesting

  1. Click the green sprout of the Reagents block (Harvest reagents).

  2. Choose the Area: suited to your tradition (1 dram per 2 hits) or not (1 per 4) (Core Rulebook p. 317).

  3. Roll the dice (Alchemy + Magic [Mental]), then click Update the reagents on the card: the harvest is added to the stock.

House Rules — Book options: reagent rules

The Reagent rules setting (Magic tab of Shadowrun settings) stays by default on the Core Rulebook. Shadow Spells adds stocks of refined and radical reagents and orichalcum, and refining (Shadow Spells p. 16) and (Street Grimoire p. 209-211); Forbidden Arcana adds a Limit and Drain bonus depending on the tier (Forbidden Arcana p. 187-191). Changing it reloads the world; the stocks already filled become raw reagents.

What the system does on its own

  • It keeps the list of a ritual's participants, the tradition penalty, the group's help and one Drain per person.

  • It creates the preparation, tracks its Potency with the clock and refuses a spent preparation.

  • It removes the drams spent and adds the harvest.

What the GM does by hand

  • The leader's glitch and the failure of a ritual along the way (a participant who leaves the foundation) (Core Rulebook p. 296).

  • What speeds up the loss of Potency, and the regrowth time of a harvested area.

All

What it is for

An Awakened character who initiates gains a grade and chooses a metamagic; many follow a mentor spirit. The system keeps the grade, applies the metamagics and masteries it can automate, and gives the mentor its bonuses, its disadvantage and the test to resist it. The Karma cost of initiation and the ordeal stay with the table (Core Rulebook p. 324).

Backlinks: @UUID[.n57naBPmfmmiiOB3]{MENU}

← @UUID[.khseU5xlrCvkbXqa]{Related settings and references} · @UUID[.ltBs1rCYjkW6Lfvg]{The grade and metamagics} →

1. In the magic tab, left column, set the Initiation Grade: right-click to raise it, left-click to lower it (see the figure of chapter @UUID[.L8wj3Cf3WQVKImL5]{4.1}, marker ①).

  2. Add the chosen metamagic with the + of the Metamagics block, or drag it from a compendium (the Mégapack provides a large selection).

  3. Click its pin, Activate Metamagic: as long as it is not activated, its effects do not play.

What the system does with an active metamagic: Shaping adds its line to the window of area spells (@UUID[.jaRKuOQo9qZOsEmZ]{area spells}); Anchoring is set on the preparation (@UUID[.QPF0DcJrinmQGnvJ]{preparations}); Structured Spellcasting removes 1 from spells' Drain, in exchange for Edge and reagents no longer raising the Limit; Harmonious Defense gives a spell defense pool visible in the Astral Plane block (Forbidden Arcana p. 43-46). The metamagics that depend on the GM's judgment stay as text on their sheet.

Forbidden Arcana's magical masteries (Mage Hunter, Death Dealer, Illusionist…) are qualities: place it, tick it active, and its level is its rating (Forbidden Arcana p. 30-42). Those that are automated add a box or a line in the relevant spell's window (for example Mage Hunter, unticked by default).

What supplement magic adds

  • Rapid-Fire Caster: reckless spellcasting without the Drain increase, one use per day and per level, counted on the sheet ("1/2 today"); Electromancer: the target's Initiative drops by half the net hits, after its resistance; Guru: the ritual window accepts ordinary participants (Forbidden Arcana p. 35-38).

  • Improved Astral Form and Astralnaut metamagics: the projection duration is shown on the sheet; Rapid Necro-Summoning: summoning Drain of 4 at least (Forbidden Arcana p. 44-45).

  • The Mystic Aptitude and Purity State adept powers (Better Than Bad p. 159); the Dark Magic tradition is recognized (Dark Terrors p. 165).

← @UUID[.zibQ5EI5pAW7Wv7E]{4.5 Initiation} · @UUID[.U12MAwTB5kUb8XGV]{The mentor spirit} →

The mentor lives in two items: the Mentor Spirit quality (the 5 Karma positive quality that is bought, Core Rulebook p. 76) and a Mentor Spirit item that carries the bonuses, the disadvantage and the resistance test. The quality points to the item in its link field; it is the item's effects that play.

Step by step: giving a character a mentor

  1. In the Mentor spirits block of the magic tab, click the +: a New mentor spirit item appears. You can also drag a mentor from the Mégapack, which provides them ready-made (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.LY0gP2n4uytah6mP.JournalEntryPage.Qp5FrYdO1ggybgHp]{the Mégapack}).

  2. Open the character's Mentor Spirit quality and link it to that item. As long as they are not linked, the sheet says so plainly: "Mentor Spirit quality missing" or "Mentor Spirit: choose a mentor".

  3. On the item's sheet, configuration tab, set the Resistance threshold, the Resistance test attributes (Charisma + Willpower by default, the test most of the book's mentors ask for (Core Rulebook p. 321-323)) and, for an adept, the Free Power Points. A mystic adept chooses once and for all the Mystic adept path (Core Rulebook p. 321).

  4. In the effects tab, file each bonus in its Mentor block: all, magician, adept or disadvantage. A "+2 if…" bonus is ticked Situational: it will be offered as a box in the window of the relevant roll.

To resist the disadvantage, click the die on the mentor's line, in the Mentor spirits block: the test is rolled against the threshold, and the card says Disadvantage resisted or not.

Your old mentors as qualities (GM)

An old "Mentor spirit (Bear) [Magician]" quality that carries its own effects still works. To move to the two-item model, the GM runs the conversion command: a window offers The selected actor or All actors in the world; the conversion creates the mentor item, files the effects in it, links the quality and whispers a summary to the GM, without deleting anything. The Mégapack provides the ready-made macro (GM's macros compendium), along with the one that undoes the conversion. The detail and the commands: wiki: Mentors, metamagics and masteries.

The system only keeps one mentor (the first) and makes the mentor inert, disadvantage included, when Magic drops to 0 (Core Rulebook p. 76) and (Core Rulebook p. 321).

House Rules — Book option: the Mentor's Mask

The Mask of the mentor setting (Magic tab of Shadowrun settings) is unticked by default. Ticked, a Mask box appears on the mentor item: a magician then reduces all their Drains by 1 (never below 2), an adept gains 1 power point (Forbidden Arcana p. 182). The system extends it: a mystic adept who chose the Adept path also gets the −1 to Drain when they cast a spell.

All

What it is for

The technomancer acts in the Matrix without a device, through Resonance. The system gives them a living persona, rolls the threading of complex forms with their Fading, compiles and registers sprites, and applies the chosen stream. This chapter covers Resonance; what belongs to the Matrix itself (marks, Matrix actions, PAN crown) is described in part 5 (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.CKM0UvZC23LLnCgv.JournalEntryPage.4tswtGQqbgDVe9IS]{the PAN crown}).

  • ① Resonance Actions: compile, decompile, register a sprite, kill a complex form, erase a resonance signature; a click on the pool rolls the test (Core Rulebook p. 250).

  • ② Complex forms: the pool threads the form; the L (level) and H (hits) columns fill in at the roll.

  • ③ Fading: the form's value at the level shown, stream included.

  • ④ Compiled sprites: tasks left, level, registered or not.

  • ⑤ Echoes: like a metamagic, an echo is placed in this block and activated by its pin.

Step by step: threading a complex form

  1. Target the token aimed at if needed, then click the complex form's dice pool. The Thread window opens.

  2. Choose the Level: the Final Fading, at the bottom, follows at once (Core Rulebook p. 251). The Distance to target sets itself from the tokens, and its noise counts in the pool.

  3. Roll the dice. The card offers to resist Fading, and to the target to defend when the form calls for it.

Fading never goes below 2 (Core Rulebook p. 251). It is Stun, and Physical when the hits exceed your Resonance (Core Rulebook p. 251).

Step by step: compiling a sprite

  1. Click the dice pool of Compile Sprite. In the window, choose the Level and the Sprite Type (Companion, Courier, Crack, Data, Fault, Generalist, Machine).

  2. Roll the dice. The GM clicks Sprite Resistance: the sprite resists with its level.

  3. On the resistance card, resist Fading (twice the sprite's hits, 2 at minimum (Core Rulebook p. 254)), then click Compile Sprite. The sprite joins the Compiled sprites block with as many tasks as net hits.

  4. The Call sprite button on its line creates the sprite's actor, as for a spirit (@UUID[.gzozcTxn5gRmcqKe]{spirits}). Register Sprite and Decompile Sprite are rolled from the Resonance actions (Core Rulebook p. 254-256), with the sprite targeted. Registering is limited by the targeted sprite's Level (without a target, Resonance), decompiling by your Social limit (Core Rulebook p. 250). Effects that modify the limit of threading, compiling or registering (a paragon, "Dissonance-marked") are added to it, and the card shows them (Kill Code p. 100, 104).

A sprite's sheet opens on the Sprite Attributes block: Level, Device Rating, Resonance and mental attributes, all equal to the Level (Core Rulebook p. 254), each clickable for an attribute test. Its attack and skill pools read Level, as in the book. A sheet whose layout the GM customized keeps its own, without the block.

← @UUID[.XDWuktzRLFwZCVWp]{Related settings and references} · @UUID[.lBOKOkF9FhWSl8UU]{Living persona, submersion and streams} →

• The living persona: every technomancer has one, as a device on the sheet, whose rating is their Resonance; the connected GM creates it if it is missing, and it cannot be deleted (Core Rulebook p. 251). It acts as the master of the PAN crown, and its Matrix damage is ticked as Stun on the sheet (Core Rulebook p. 228).

  • The submersion grade is set in the device tab of the left column (Submersion Grade, right or left click); echoes are placed in the Echoes block.

  • The streams of Kill Code (Cyberadept, Machinist, Sourcerer, Technoshaman, and the dissonant streams) are qualities (Kill Code p. 89-93) and (Kill Code p. 133-134). The system applies their effects: Fading reduced by 2 for the forms the stream knows (it can then go down to 1), +2 dice to compile and decompile two types of sprites, and the stream's "daemon" according to the submersion grade. A Machinist's living persona acts as a rigger command console (@UUID[Compendium.sr5.manual.JournalEntry.5afKb26kGAzDG0I9.JournalEntryPage.FhRTLAI7RMJ8TvTP]{the rigger console}), but only shares the autosofts that one of their Resonance [Program] echoes copies; the echo carries the name of the program copied (Core Rulebook p. 258, Kill Code p. 91).

  • Great form sprites: the compiling window of a Technoshaman, and of her alone, carries the Major form box. Ticked, the compiling Fading doubles, and the sprite carries its type's power in its description; this power is played from that text (Kill Code p. 92-93).

Where to find the streams?

A stream only acts if it carries its system effect (Special case category, value "Stream: …"). The Mégapack's stream qualities carry it in their recent versions; on an older quality, the GM adds it in the effects tab. The detail: wiki: Matrix, AI, devices and vehicles.

What the system does on its own

  • It computes the Fading of each form and of each compilation, stream included, and chooses its damage type.

  • It rolls the sprites' resistance, counts their tasks, creates the sprite and its actor.

  • It keeps the living persona and applies the streams' effects.

What the GM does by hand

  • Great form powers, played from the sprite's description; submersion itself (Karma, ordeal).

  • Making sure a stream's complex form goes to the right stream: stream forms are compendium items, the system does not check who buys them.
